test_cases.title: IMU Sample Rate at 200 Hz
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock MPU-6050 with deterministic register fixtures. Drive the library through a synthetic 1-second tick schedule.
procedure: Initialize the IMU library and complete startup probe.
Drive the library tick loop for exactly 1.0 simulated second.
Count the number of IMU sample structures published by the library.
Compute the average inter-sample period from sample timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly 200 samples are produced in 1.0 simulated second and the average inter-sample period equals 5.0 ms within +/- 1 percent.

test_cases.title: Accelerometer Range Configured to plus or minus 16 G
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock MPU-6050 that records all register writes to ACCEL_CONFIG (0x1C).
procedure: Initialize the IMU library.
Read the recorded value written to the ACCEL_CONFIG register from the mock.
Decode the AFS_SEL field (bits 4:3) of the recorded byte.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: ACCEL_CONFIG AFS_SEL field equals 0b11 (selecting plus or minus 16 G full scale) per MPU-6050 datasheet.

test_cases.title: Gyroscope Range Configured to plus or minus 2000 dps
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock MPU-6050 that records all register writes to GYRO_CONFIG (0x1B).
procedure: Initialize the IMU library.
Read the recorded value written to the GYRO_CONFIG register from the mock.
Decode the FS_SEL field (bits 4:3) of the recorded byte.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: GYRO_CONFIG FS_SEL field equals 0b11 (selecting plus or minus 2000 dps full scale) per MPU-6050 datasheet.

test_cases.title: Accelerometer Output in Meters per Second Squared
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library with mock returning a known raw accelerometer reading equivalent to 1.0 G on the Z axis at +/- 16 G full scale (raw = 2048 LSB).
procedure: Inject the fixed raw accelerometer reading into the mock register file.
Trigger one IMU sample read.
Read the published accelerometer Z value from the IMU sample structure.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Published accelerometer Z equals 9.80665 m/s^2 within +/- 0.05 m/s^2; X and Y axes equal 0.0 m/s^2 within +/- 0.05 m/s^2.

test_cases.title: Gyroscope Output in Radians per Second
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library with mock returning a known raw gyroscope reading equivalent to 1000 dps on the X axis at +/- 2000 dps full scale (raw = 16384 LSB).
procedure: Inject the fixed raw gyroscope reading into the mock register file.
Trigger one IMU sample read.
Read the published gyroscope X value from the IMU sample structure.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Published gyroscope X equals 17.4533 rad/s (1000 dps) within +/- 0.01 rad/s; Y and Z axes equal 0.0 rad/s within +/- 0.01 rad/s.

test_cases.title: Per-Sample Timestamp Present and Monotonic
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock with simulated monotonic clock advancing at 5 ms per tick.
procedure: Drive the IMU library tick loop for 100 consecutive samples.
Collect each published IMU sample and record its timestamp field.
Verify every sample contains a non-zero timestamp.
Verify timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 100 samples contain a populated timestamp field, timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing, and consecutive deltas equal 5 ms within +/- 1 percent.

test_cases.title: Body-Frame Axis Convention Inspection
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library with a sequence of mock readings representing accelerometer responses to known orientations relative to the documented X-forward, Y-right, Z-down body frame.
procedure: Inject a mock raw reading representing 1 G applied along body +X (nose up under gravity).
Read the published sample and record accelerometer X, Y, Z.
Inject a mock raw reading representing 1 G applied along body +Y (right-wing down under gravity).
Read the published sample and record accelerometer X, Y, Z.
Inject a mock raw reading representing 1 G applied along body +Z (upright on pad under gravity).
Read the published sample and record accelerometer X, Y, Z.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Published accelerometer values match the X-forward, Y-right, Z-down body-frame convention for each injection: +X axis returns +9.80665 on X only, +Y axis returns +9.80665 on Y only, +Z axis returns +9.80665 on Z only, all within +/- 0.05 m/s^2.

test_cases.title: Power-On Self-Test Pass on Healthy Device
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock MPU-6050 returning the expected WHO_AM_I value (0x68) on register 0x75.
procedure: Invoke the IMU library startup sequence.
Capture the POST result reported by the library.
Capture how many times the WHO_AM_I register was read.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: POST reports pass, the WHO_AM_I register is read exactly once during startup, and the library transitions to the operational state.

test_cases.title: Power-On Self-Test Fail on Wrong Device
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock MPU-6050 returning an incorrect WHO_AM_I value (0x00) on register 0x75.
procedure: Invoke the IMU library startup sequence.
Capture the POST result reported by the library.
Read the IMU health field after startup completes.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: POST reports fail and the published IMU health state is unhealthy.

test_cases.title: Continuous Health Reporting Across Mission Tick Loop
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock returning healthy responses, with health-reporting hook subscribed.
procedure: Drive the IMU library tick loop for 1000 consecutive samples.
On every tick, read the IMU health field reported by the library.
Count the number of ticks for which a health value was reported.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: A health value is reported on every one of the 1000 ticks (no gaps), and all values are healthy.

test_cases.title: Unhealthy Marking on Sample Read Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock that succeeds at startup but fails subsequent register-burst reads with an I2C/SPI error.
procedure: Complete startup and verify health is initially healthy.
Configure the mock to fail the next register-burst read.
Drive one IMU library tick.
Read the IMU health field reported by the library.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: After the failed read, the published IMU health state transitions to unhealthy.

test_cases.title: Continuation After Sample Read Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock that succeeds at startup, fails one read, then resumes returning valid samples.
procedure: Complete startup successfully.
Drive 10 ticks with mock returning valid samples.
Configure the mock to fail the next read once.
Drive one tick (which fails).
Configure the mock to resume returning valid samples.
Drive 10 additional ticks.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The library does not abort, exit, or assert; 20 valid samples are produced across the pre-failure and post-failure intervals; tick cadence is preserved.

test_cases.title: Unhealthy Recovery Latching Behavior on Persistent Failures
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock; configure mock to fail reads continuously for 50 consecutive ticks.
procedure: Complete startup successfully.
Configure the mock to fail every subsequent read.
Drive 50 IMU library ticks.
Record the published health value on each tick.
Confirm the library remains running (no crash or exit) at the end.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Health is reported as unhealthy on every tick where reads fail, and the library continues to execute through all 50 ticks without aborting.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence (Shared Logic Layer)
test_cases.setup: Compile the IMU library shared logic layer twice: once against the POSIX HAL adapter and once against the Pico2 HAL adapter (both running on host via host-build of Pico2 sources). Drive both with an identical scripted mock register-response sequence.
procedure: Initialize both POSIX-built and Pico2-built libraries with identical configuration.
Feed both libraries the same scripted sequence of 1000 raw register responses.
Collect the published IMU sample stream from each build.
Compare the two sample streams field-by-field (timestamp, accel XYZ, gyro XYZ, health).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The two streams are bit-identical for accel/gyro values and health flags, and timestamps differ only by the deterministic clock-source offset documented in the design.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Output Across Repeated Runs
test_cases.setup: Initialize IMU library against POSIX mock with a fixed scripted register-response sequence and a fixed simulated clock.
procedure: Run the IMU library against the scripted sequence; record all 1000 published IMU samples to buffer A.
Reset the library, mock, and simulated clock to identical initial state.
Run the IMU library against the same scripted sequence; record all 1000 published IMU samples to buffer B.
Compare buffers A and B byte-for-byte.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Buffer A equals buffer B byte-for-byte across all 1000 samples (timestamps, accel, gyro, health all identical).

test_cases.title: POST Hardware Demonstration on Pico2 Target
test_cases.setup: Flash the FT1 firmware build to a Pico 2 board with an MPU-6050 IMU connected per the FT1 wiring diagram. Open a serial terminal at 115200 baud.
procedure: Power on the Pico 2 board with the IMU connected and verify the boot banner appears on the serial terminal.
Observe the IMU POST log line printed during startup.
Record the serial terminal output to a log file.
Power off the board, disconnect the IMU SDA line, and power the board back on.
Observe the IMU POST log line during this second boot.
Record the second serial terminal output to a log file.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: First boot logs IMU POST PASS with subsequent healthy state; second boot (IMU disconnected) logs IMU POST FAIL with the published health state reporting unhealthy.

test_cases.title: Pico2 Build IMU Stream Demonstration
test_cases.setup: Flash the FT1 firmware build (Pico2 target) to a Pico 2 with MPU-6050 attached. Open a serial terminal at 115200 baud and enable IMU sample logging.
procedure: Power on the Pico 2 board.
Wait for IMU POST PASS log line.
Capture serial output for 10 seconds while the board sits stationary on a level surface.
Save the captured serial stream as a CSV of (timestamp, ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, health).
Plot timestamp deltas across all captured samples.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: CSV contains approximately 2000 samples (200 Hz x 10 s) within +/- 1 percent, every row carries a populated monotonic timestamp, accelerometer Z reads +9.80665 m/s^2 within +/- 0.5 m/s^2, gyro magnitudes are below 0.1 rad/s, and health is healthy on every row.
